item.title: matomo: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA bundle
item.description:
Part of #576541.

Matomo has a bundled CA file, vendor/composer/ca-bundle/res/cacert.pem. By default, Matomo gives this file to curl for each request. Matomo does not try a CA bundle of the system first. This change replaces the installed file with a symlink to the ca-no-trust-rules-bundle.crt file of cacert in installPhase. Thus, the installed file is a symlink to cacert, and replaceDependencies can replace cacert. This change also adds the file to filesToFix. Thus, postFixup writes the length and SHA-256 value of the new file into config/manifest.inc.php, and Matomo uses these values to examine its files.

item.title: temurin-bin: generate cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

Heads up, most of this change is a reindent – you can press "hide whitespace" in the diff to make it easier to read.

The Temurin binary JDKs, temurin-bin and temurin-jre-bin, have a bundled Java trust store, lib/security/cacerts. This change makes a new cacerts from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts, as the merged openjdk change #576518 does. temurin-bin is also the bootstrap JDK of openjdk. Thus, this change adds the argument regenerateCacerts, and openjdk sets it to false for its bootstrap JDK. The drvPath of each openjdk does not change. This change does not change jmods/java.base.jmod or the darwin packages.

The JDKs semeru-bin and semeru-jre-bin also come from temurin-bin/jdk-linux-base.nix. At this time, their JVM does not start on nixpkgs, and it shows this error: cannot enable executable stack as shared object requires: Invalid argument. This occurs because glibc 2.41 and newer versions do not accept a library that must have an executable stack, and libj9vm29.so is such a library. Thus, it is not possible to use keytool at build time. This change sets regenerateCacerts = false for these two packages, and their drvPath does not change. The repair of these two packages (a new version, or meta.broken) is a different task.
